description:
Pastor and theologian Dr. Brant Bosserman (Trinitas Church) returns to discuss his upcoming article in the Westminster Theological Journal titled "The Lord's Day and the Maximalist Tendency in Romans 14:5-6" where he argues that the strongest explanation for the dispute over holy days reflected in Romans 14:5-6 is the early establishment of the first day of the week as the undisputed time of Christian assembly. Despite their differences about which foods qualified as clean, maximalists and minimalists were united on the Lord’s Day at the Lord’s Supper.  So long as both partook of the Lord’s Supper together and resolved to eat their every meal in consistency with the thanksgiving pronounced with the sacrament (Romans 14:6c, e), they could carry on as one worshiping body.

We will discuss his central arguments, what is going on in Romans 14, and how the historical context surrounding the text supports the universal Christian practice of corporately gathering for worship on the first day.
